label: SpO₂
why: Low oxygen saturation can mean hypoxia from a cabin atmosphere fault, fire or smoke.
howDecided: Rule SPO-01: SpO₂ < 94 % → caution. Earth clinical convention, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §4).
next: Re-measure: warm your hands, sit still for 1 minute, finger fully in, hand at heart level. Still below 94 % → tell the CMO now.

label: SpO₂
why: Low oxygen saturation can mean hypoxia from a cabin atmosphere fault, fire or smoke.
howDecided: Rule SPO-02: SpO₂ < 90 % → warning. Earth clinical convention, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §4).

label: PVT median
what: Your PVT median is above {limit} ms, {percent} % slower than your pre-flight baseline ({baseline} ms).
why: PVT slows early in flight in ISS crews, and nights of 6 h or less of sleep slow it further. Slower attention raises the risk of performance errors.
howDecided: Rule COG-01: PVT median > {limit} ms (pre-flight baseline {baseline} ms + {percent} %) → caution. The baseline is a synthetic pre-loaded profile; +{percent} % is a team heuristic, not a NASA limit. No adaptation corridor yet.
next: Tell the CMO today and repeat the test tomorrow morning.
